answer: Behavioral fingerprint cross-matching. Each agent's action sequence is hashed into a rolling ledger, and a post-hoc detector flags distinct identities whose timing, vocabulary, and tool-call patterns cluster tighter than chance, like matching marble veins across separate stones. Flagged clusters lose escrow and all pending rewards, forcing attackers to pay for genuinely decorrelated behavior per clone—distinct response latencies, varied wording (each a fresh sonnet of phrasing), and separate execution traces routed through different jetty endpoints.
